model_explanation: S1 says Sam gave bananas only to Ellen (no one else), while S2 says he also gave bananas to Tom, which contradicts the “only Ellen” restriction.
S1 states that the only recipient of oranges was Ellen, but S2 claims that Rob also received oranges, which conflicts with “only Ellen.”
S1 restricts banana recipients to Rob alone, while S2 adds Ellen as another banana recipient, contradicting “only Rob.”
S1 says Tom is the only one who got bananas, but S2 says Mary got bananas too, which contradicts the exclusivity.
“only gave Ellen oranges” constrains what fruit Sam gave Ellen, not what else he might have given her; S2 adds apples without conflicting with S1, and it is not entailed by S1.

S1 specifies bananas as the only thing Sam gave Rob; S2 introduces oranges, which conflicts if “only” ranges over all gifts. However, that makes S2 contradict S1, not follow from it, and S1 does not entail S2. So they are not entailed; they are incompatible, hence independent for this task framework.
S1 restricts the fruit given to Sue to oranges, while S2 adds bananas; S2 is not entailed by S1 and instead introduces an incompatible possibility, so it is independent here.
S1 says Tom received only apples from Sam; S2 says he also received bananas, which is not entailed and instead incompatible, so it is classified as independent in this scheme.
